hints: Focus on what hot concentrated acidified KMnO4 does, it cleaves the C=C double bond completely to give acids, ketones or CO2.
Draw methylpropanoic acid, $(CH_3)_2CHCOOH$, and notice the $COOH$ carbon must have come from one end of the old C=C bond.
Since it is the only organic product, join two identical acid fragments back together at their $COOH$ carbons to rebuild a symmetrical C=C.
walkthrough:
**Recall oxidative cleavage**

Think of hot concentrated $KMnO_4$ as chemical scissors. It cuts right through the C=C and turns each alkene carbon into its own product.

Rule: $RCH=CHR' \rightarrow RCOOH + R'COOH$ (each $=CH-$ becomes $-COOH$)

**Analyse the given product**

Methylpropanoic acid is 2-methylpropanoic acid, $(CH_3)_2CHCOOH$.

It has 4 carbons in total: $$(CH_3)_2CH-COOH$$ The $COOH$ carbon is the old alkene carbon.

**Use the only product clue**

Only one organic product means both halves of the alkene were identical. The alkene must be symmetrical.

So we need: $$2 \times \text{C}_4 \text{ acid from one C}_8 \text{ symmetrical alkene}$$

**Rebuild the alkene**

Remove the O atoms from two $COOH$ groups and join the two carbons with a double bond:
$$ (CH_3)_2CH-COOH + HOOC-CH(CH_3)_2 \rightarrow (CH_3)_2CH-CH=CH-CH(CH_3)_2 $$
This is $CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH=CH-CH(CH_3)-CH_3$, which is 2,5-dimethylhex-3-ene.

options.A: 2,5-dimethylhex-3-ene is $(CH_3)_2CHCH=CHCH(CH_3)_2$. It is symmetrical about the C3=C4 bond. Cleavage gives two moles of $(CH_3)_2CHCOOH$, which is methylpropanoic acid as the only organic product.
options.B: 2-methylbut-2-ene is $(CH_3)_2C=CHCH_3$. It is unsymmetrical. Cleavage gives propanone, $(CH_3)_2C=O$, from the $(CH_3)_2C=$ end plus ethanoic acid, $CH_3COOH$, from the $=CHCH_3$ end. Two different products, so incorrect.
options.C: Methylpropene is $(CH_3)_2C=CH_2$. Cleavage gives propanone, $(CH_3)_2C=O$, plus carbon dioxide from the $=CH_2$ end which is fully oxidised. No carboxylic acid with 4 carbons is formed.
options.D: Oct-4-ene is $CH_3CH_2CH_2CH=CHCH_2CH_2CH_3$. It is symmetrical and does give a single acid, but it gives butanoic acid, $CH_3CH_2CH_2COOH$, not branched methylpropanoic acid. This is the trap for students who spot symmetry but ignore branching.
